rationale: FS-P9 (fsharp lane, 2026-10-08) — A MUTUAL TYPE GROUP IS SEVERAL TYPES IN ONE NODE, and the lane read it as one. F# writes `type A = … and B = …` for types that refer to each other, and the grammar emits ONE `type_definition` holding a clause body per type (`type_abbrev_defn`, `anon_type_defn`, `record_type_defn`, `union_type_defn`, `interface_type_defn`, `enum_type_defn`, `delegate_type_defn`, and the bodyless `type_declaration`). Every name in the analyzer's type branch was read with `findDescendant(node, "type_name")` — the FIRST name in the whole definition — so the group was named after its first clause whichever one the source meant, and every later clause's members were published under that name. Measured on the 3,000-file draw (.tmp-probe/fs-p10-groups.mts, arm rows-pass13-meta.ndjson): 79 groups in 67 files, 182 clauses after a first, **161 of those names published nowhere** — Bolero.Html's `ElementBuilder`, `ComponentBuilder`, `ComponentWithAttrsBuilder` (their members attributed to `ConcatBuilder`), Argu's `IFunc`/`ITemplateFunc`, Deedle's `address`. THE HALF A MISSING-NAME COUNT CANNOT SEE IS THE ATTRIBUTION, and it is the worse half: `ConcatBuilder.GroupOwn` is a published symbol, so a containment edge or a call that lands on it RESOLVES, and nothing downstream can tell it names the wrong type. Every row below therefore pins an OWNER, not only a name. The four shapes are here because they reach the type branch by different arms: (1) abbreviation + class, where the pre-fix file published `GroupAbbrev` only — `GroupReal`, `GroupReal.GroupCall` and `GroupReal.GroupOwn` all attributed to the abbreviation, and the `extends` edge named `GroupAbbrev -> GroupBase`; (2) record + record, where the declared-type arm climbed from the field to the DEFINITION and took the first `type_name`, publishing the second record's field type as the first's; (3) union + union, the same defect through the DU-case arm; (4) a BODYLESS clause whose attribute is written BETWEEN the clauses — Deedle's `type Address = int64<address>` + `and [<Measure>] address`, where the `attributes` node is a direct child of the GROUP rather than of the clause it applies to, so the clause frame has to carry it by POSITION (pre-fix `groupMeasure` was published nowhere and the `uses` edge for `Measure` named `GroupAddress`). The fix is not a second copy of the type branch: each clause is pushed as a walk frame marked `asTypeUnit` and the same branch admits it, so the kind classifier, the record fields, the DU/enum cases, the interface implementations, the `extends` edges, the member scoping and the containment composition are the SAME code for a clause and for a whole definition. The forbid half is the pre-fix shape of each of those arms, spelled the way the pre-fix analyzer spelled it (fqns read off the pre-fix dump, not guessed): a forbid row must be written in the spelling a REGRESSION would emit, which is what makes it fire on the return of the rule rather than never. The two `expectRelationshipCount` pins are exact totals, because a per-row expect can only say 'at least one' and this defect's other half was a COUNT of edges that moved owner together.

expectSymbols.name: GroupAbbrev
expectSymbols.note: clause 1 of shape (1): the abbreviation. It published pre-fix too — as the name of the WHOLE group.

expectSymbols.name: GroupReal
expectSymbols.note: clause 2 of shape (1): the type the pre-fix analyzer never minted at all, and whose members it published under `GroupAbbrev`.

expectSymbols.name: GroupSecondRecord
expectSymbols.note: shape (2): the second record. Pre-fix its field was published under `GroupRecord`.

expectSymbols.name: groupMeasure
expectSymbols.note: shape (4): the bodyless `and [<Measure>] groupMeasure` clause. Pre-fix it was published NOWHERE, and the measure marker that decides its kind is an `attributes` sibling BETWEEN the clauses, not a child of the clause.

expectRelationships.note: the member is contained by the type that declares it — pre-fix the parent was `Fixture.MutualType.GroupAbbrev`
shape (4) end to end: the bodyless clause is a type this file declares and contains
the inherit belongs to the second clause

the record-field arm's owner: read from the RECORD CLAUSE, not from the definition's first `type_name`. A class-field annotation on the same defect class was already owner-by-position; this arm and that one answer the same question and had different answers.
the attribute usage is read INSIDE the clause it applies to, because the clause frame carries the group's `attributes` siblings by position

expectRelationshipCount.note: exact: 3 dependency types + 8 clauses + 6 members/fields/cases. A per-row expect says 'at least one'; the pre-fix defect MOVED edges between owners rather than deleting them, and only an exact total states that

forbidRelationships.note: PRE-FIX shape (1): the class's member contained by the abbreviation — the misplaced owner, spelled the way the pre-fix analyzer spelled it
PRE-FIX shape (2): the second record's field under the first record
PRE-FIX shape (3): the second union's case under the first union
PRE-FIX shape (1): the inherit edge named the first clause, because the first clause's name was the one in scope for the whole group

PRE-FIX shape (2), the declared-type half: the second record's field type published as the first record's dependency. This is a DETERMINATE edge naming a declaration that is definitively not the one the annotation sits in — worse than an ambiguous target, because the wrongness is asserted
PRE-FIX shape (4): the `Measure` usage attributed to the group's FIRST clause, because the attribute node was walked in the definition's scope
